questions.text:
थोक व्यापार की निम्नलिखित विशेषताओं को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
i. इसका गठन अनेक बिचौलिए, सौदागरों और पूर्तिघरों द्वारा होता है
ii. थोक विक्रेता प्रायः फुटकर भंडारों को उधार देते हैं
iii. सामान्यतः फुटकर विक्रेता अधिकतर थोक विक्रेता की पूँजी पर कार्य करते हैं
iv. डाक आदेश, स्वचालित बिक्री मशीनें, फेरी वाले इसके कुछ उदाहरण हैं
विकल्प :
(A) केवल i, ii और iii सही हैं।
(B) केवल ii, iii और iv सही हैं।
(C) केवल i, iii और iv सही हैं।
(D) केवल i, ii और iv सही हैं।
questions.text_english:
Read the following characteristics of wholesale trading carefully and choose the correct option:
i. It is constituted by numerous intermediaries, merchants and supply houses.
ii. Wholesalers often extend credit to retail stores.
iii. Generally retailers operate very largely on the wholesaler's capital.
iv. Mail order, automatic vending machines, street vendors are some of its examples.
Option:
(A) Only i, ii and iii are correct.
(B) Only ii, iii and iv are correct.
(C) Only i, iii and iv are correct.
(D) Only i, ii and iv are correct.

options.A: केवल i, ii और iii सही हैं।
options.B: केवल ii, iii और iv सही हैं।
options.C: केवल i, iii और iv सही हैं।
options.D: केवल i, ii और iv सही हैं।

options_english.A: Only i, ii and iii are correct.
options_english.B: Only ii, iii and iv are correct.
options_english.C: Only i, iii and iv are correct.
options_english.D: Only i, ii and iv are correct.

questions.solution: Option (A) is correct because statements i, ii, and iii accurately describe wholesale trading. Statement iv is incorrect because mail order, automatic vending machines, and street vendors are examples of retail trade, not wholesale trade.

questions.text_english:
Which one of the following is the headquarter of the 'World Trade Organization'?
(A) New York
(B) Delhi
(C) Geneva
(D) London
questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. The World Trade Organization (WTO) is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. New York houses the UN, Delhi is the capital of India, and London is the capital of the UK, none of which are the WTO headquarters.

questions.text:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गये हैं। ये अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) हैं। दोनों कथनों को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए ।
अभिकथन (A) : अयस्क पर आधारित उद्योग कच्चे माल के स्रोत के समीप स्थित हैं।
कारण (R) : उद्योग परिवहन लागत घटाकर लाभ को बढ़ाते हैं।
विकल्प :
(A) (A) सही है और (R) गलत है।
(B) (A) गलत है और (R) सही है।
(C) (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
(D) (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
questions.text_english:
Two statements are given below. They are Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Read both the statements carefully and choose the correct option.
Assertion (A): Industries based on ores are located close to the sources of raw material.
Reason (R): Industries maximise profits by reducing transportation costs.
Options:
(A) (A) is correct and (R) is false.
(B) (A) is false and (R) is correct.
(C) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is correct explanation of (A).
(D) Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not correct explanation of (A).

options.C: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.D: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।

options_english.C: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is correct explanation of (A).
options_english.D: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. Industries based on heavy raw materials like ores are located near the sources to minimize transportation costs, thereby maximizing profits. The reason correctly explains the location choice in the assertion.

questions.text:
भारत में नगरीय जनसंख्या की तीव्र वृद्धि दर का निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कारण गलत है ?
(A) नगरों में उच्च आर्थिक विकास ।
(B) नगरों में स्वास्थ्य संबंधी दशाओं में सुधार ।
(C) नगरीय क्षेत्रों का तेज़ी से विस्तार ।
(D) नगरों में रोज़गार के अवसरों की उपलब्धता ।
questions.text_english:
Which one of the followings is the false reason of high growth rate of urban population in India?
(A) Higher economic development in cities
(B) Improvement in health condition in cities
(C) Rapid expansion of urban areas
(D) Availability of employment opportunities in cities

options.B: नगरों में स्वास्थ्य संबंधी दशाओं में सुधार ।
options.C: नगरीय क्षेत्रों का तेज़ी से विस्तार ।
options.D: नगरों में रोज़गार के अवसरों की उपलब्धता ।

options_english.B: Improvement in health condition in cities
options_english.D: Availability of employment opportunities in cities

questions.solution: Option (B) is incorrect as a cause for high urban population *growth rate*. While health improvements are beneficial, they are not the primary driver of rapid urban population *growth* compared to migration, economic development, and expansion. Options A, C, and D are direct contributors.

questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. Goa has the highest percentage of urban population among the given states according to Census 2011 data.

questions.text:
भारत में एक कृषि फसल की विशेषताएँ नीचे दी गई हैं। इनको ध्यान से पढ़िए और फसल की पहचान कीजिए ।
यह उष्ण आर्द्र कटिबंधीय क्षेत्र की एक फसल है।
पश्चिम बंगाल के किसान एक वर्ष में इसकी तीन फ़सलें उगाते हैं।
उत्तर-पश्चिमी भागों में यह खरीफ़ फसल के रूप में उगाई जाती है।
इसके प्रमुख उत्पादक राज्य पश्चिम बंगाल, उत्तर प्रदेश और पंजाब हैं।
फसल :
(A) गेहूँ
(B) चना
(C) बाजरा
(D) चावल
questions.text_english:
The characteristics of an agricultural crop in India are given below. Read them carefully and identify the crop.
It is a crop of tropical humid area.
West Bengal farmers grow it three crops in a year.
It is grown as a Kharif crop in north-western parts.
West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh and Punjab are major producing states.
Crop:
(A) Wheat
(B) Gram
(C) Bajra
(D) Rice
questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. The characteristics described—tropical humid climate, three crops a year in West Bengal (Aman, Aus, Boro), and being a Kharif crop in north-western India—specifically identify rice (paddy).

questions.text:
नीचे दो कथन दिए गये हैं। ये अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) हैं। दोनों कथनों को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए ।
अभिकथन (A) : एक क्षेत्र का आर्थिक विकास उसके संसाधनों पर आधारित होता है।
कारण (R) : आर्थिक विकास के लिए तकनीक के साथ-साथ निवेश की आवश्यकता होती है।
विकल्प :
(A) (A) सही है, परन्तु (R) गलत है।
(B) (A) गलत है, परन्तु (R) सही है।
(C) (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
(D) (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
questions.text_english:
Two statements are given below. They are Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Read both the statements carefully and choose the correct option.
Assertion (A): The economic development of a region depends upon its resource base.
Reason (R): Economic development requires technologies as well as investment.
Options:
(A) (A) is correct, but (R) is false.
(B) (A) is false, but (R) is correct.
(C) Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(D) Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not correct explanation of (A).

options.C: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.D: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।

options_english.C: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.D: Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. Both statements are true. Resources form the basis of economic development, and technology and investment are the means to utilize these resources for development. However, the reason does not directly define or explain why the development *depends* on the resource base.

questions.text:
स्तंभ-I का मिलान स्तंभ-II से कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
स्तंभ-I (राष्ट्रीय जलमार्ग) | स्तंभ-II (नदी)
(a) राष्ट्रीय जलमार्ग संख्या 1 | (i) मातई
(b) राष्ट्रीय जलमार्ग संख्या 2 | (ii) गोदावरी
(c) राष्ट्रीय जलमार्ग संख्या 4 | (iii) गंगा
(d) राष्ट्रीय जलमार्ग संख्या 5 | (iv) ब्रह्मपुत्र
विकल्प :
(A) (iv) (iii) (ii) (i)
(B) (iv) (iii) (i) (ii)
(C) (iii) (iv) (i) (ii)
(D) (iii) (iv) (ii) (i)
questions.text_english:
Match the Column-I with Column-II and choose the correct option:
Column-I (National Waterway) | Column-II (River)
(a) National Waterway No. 1 | (i) Matai
(b) National Waterway No. 2 | (ii) Godavari
(c) National Waterway No. 4 | (iii) Ganga
(d) National Waterway No. 5 | (iv) Brahmaputra
Options:
(A) (iv) (iii) (ii) (i)
(B) (iv) (iii) (i) (ii)
(C) (iii) (iv) (i) (ii)
(D) (iii) (iv) (ii) (i)
questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. The correct matches are: NW 1 - Ganga (iii), NW 2 - Brahmaputra (iv), NW 4 - Godavari (ii), and NW 5 - Matai (i).

questions.text_english:
Which of the following is an example of a 'Modern City'?
(A) Surat
(B) Nagpur
(C) Madurai
(D) Hyderabad
questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. In the context of Indian urban history, cities like Nagpur are categorized as 'Modern' cities developed during the British period, whereas Surat, Madurai, and Hyderabad are historically classified as 'Ancient' or 'Medieval' cities.

questions.text:
भारत में गैरिसन नगर से संबंधित सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
(A) रानीगंज, डिग्बोई और झरिया
(B) महू, बबीना और उधमपुर
(C) इटारसी, कटनी और कांडला
(D) मोदीनगर, जमशेदपुर और भिलाई
questions.text_english:
Choose the correct option related to Garrison towns in India:
(A) Raniganj, Digboi and Jharia
(B) Mhow, Babina and Udhampur
(C) Itarsi, Katni and Kandla
(D) Modinagar, Jamshedpur and Bhilai
questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. Mhow, Babina, and Udhampur are well-known military cantonment or garrison towns in India. Group A are mining towns, group C are transport/port towns, and group D are industrial towns.

questions.text:
बस्ती के निम्नलिखित लक्षणों को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और बस्ती के प्रकार की पहचान कीजिए :
यह जंगलों में एकाकी झोंपड़ियों के रूप में दिखाई पड़ती है।
यह छोटी पहाड़ियों की ढालों पर दिखाई पड़ती है।
मेघालय, उत्तराखंड और हिमाचल प्रदेश के अनेक भागों में इस प्रकार की बस्तियाँ पाई जाती हैं।
बस्ती का प्रकार :
(A) आकेंद्रित
(B) विखंडित
(C) पल्लीकृत
(D) परिक्षिप्त
questions.text_english:
Read the following characteristics of settlements carefully and identify its type:
It is seen in the form of isolated huts in the forest.
It is visible on the slopes of small hills.
This kind of settlements are found in different parts of Meghalaya, Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh.
Settlement types:
(A) Nucleated
(B) Fragmented
(C) Hamleted
(D) Dispersed
questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. Dispersed settlements are characterized by isolated huts or small clusters spread across difficult terrains like hills and forests, as found in the Himalayan regions and Meghalaya.

questions.text:
रिक्त स्थानों की पूर्ति के लिए सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
भारतीय रेलवे की स्थापना 1853 में हुई तथा _______ से _______ के बीच 34 कि.मी. लंबी रेल लाइन निर्मित की गई।
(A) मुंबई (बंबई), थाणे
(B) कोलकाता (कलकत्ता), हुगली
(C) चेन्नई (मद्रास), मदुरै
(D) बेंगलूरु (बैंगलोर), कालीकट
questions.text_english:
Choose the correct option to fill the blanks:
Indian Railway was introduced in 1853 and a railway line was constructed from _______ to _______ covering a distance of 34 km.
(A) Mumbai (Bombay), Thane
(B) Kolkata (Calcutta), Hugli
(C) Chennai (Madras), Madurai
(D) Bengaluru (Bangalore), Calicut
questions.solution: The correct answer is Mumbai (Bombay) and Thane. The first railway line in India was inaugurated in 1853, connecting Bombay (now Mumbai) to Thane, covering a distance of 34 km.

questions.text_english:
Which one of the following human body system gets affected the most by water pollution?
(A) Nervous system
(B) Circulatory system
(C) Respiratory system
(D) Digestive system
questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. Water pollution introduces pathogens and harmful chemicals that primarily cause water-borne diseases like cholera, diarrhea, and typhoid, which directly impact the digestive system.

Which of the following tribes is in majority in Jhabua district of Madhya Pradesh?
(A) Bhil
(B) Tharu
(C) Bakarwal
(D) Gaddi
questions.solution: Option (A) is correct. The Bhil tribe is predominantly found in the Jhabua district of Madhya Pradesh and is known for its distinct cultural identity.

In which of the following stage/stages, the natural growth of population was/were almost stagnant?
(A) Only I
(B) Only II
(C) Only I and Last
(D) Only II and Last
questions.instruction_line: Read the given passage and answer the Q. Nos. 15 to 17
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the given passage and answer the Q. Nos. 15 to 17
questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. According to Demographic Transition Theory, population is stagnant in Stage I (due to high fertility and high mortality balancing each other) and in the Last Stage (due to low fertility and low mortality).

questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. According to the passage, the second stage is characterized by a significant decline in mortality due to improvements in health and sanitation conditions.

(B) Bangladesh
(C) Japan

questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. Bangladesh is widely considered to be in the demographic transition stage where mortality has declined significantly, while fertility is also beginning to decline, which characterizes the second/third transition phase.

आर्थिक विकास की आरंभिक अवस्थाओं में लोगों का एक बड़ा अनुपात प्राथमिक सेक्टर में कार्य करता था । एक विकसित अर्थव्यवस्था में बहुसंख्यक श्रमिक तृतीयक क्रियाकलापों में रोज़गार पाते हैं और अपेक्षाकृत कम संख्या में द्वितीयक सेक्टर में कार्यरत होते हैं।

Tertiary Sector
When you fall ill you go to your family doctor or you call a doctor. Sometimes your parents take you to a hospital for treatment. While in school, you are taught by your teachers. In the event of any dispute, legal opinion is obtained from a lawyer. Likewise, there are many professionals who provide their services against payment of their fee. Thus, all types of services are special skills provided in exchange of payments. Health, education, law, governance and recreation etc. require professional skills. These services require other theoretical knowledge and practical training. Tertiary activities are related to the service sector. Manpower is an important component of the service sector as most of the tertiary activities are performed by skilled labour, professionally trained experts and consultants.
In the initial stages of economic development, larger proportion of people worked in the primary sector. In a developed economy, the majority of workers get employment in tertiary activity and a moderate proportion is employed in the secondary sector.

questions.text_english:
(a) How do differences in national resources become the basis of international trade? Explain with examples.
OR
(b) Explain the differences between the inland and out-ports with examples.

key_points: Geological structure, climate, and mineral resources create comparative advantage.
Countries export what they have in surplus and import what they lack (e.g., Oil from Middle East, Minerals from Australia).

questions.solution: National resources are unevenly distributed due to differences in geological structure, mineral wealth, and climate, which form the primary basis for international trade. For instance, countries with surplus mineral resources like Saudi Arabia export petroleum, while countries lacking such resources import them. This comparative advantage drives global exchange, as nations specialize in producing goods that utilize their abundant resources efficiently, leading to inter-dependent trade patterns. Without these geographical and resource variations, international trade would be significantly limited as all countries would be self-sufficient in the same types of goods.

key_points: Strengthening water security through community participation.
Promoting water conservation and artificial recharge techniques.
Encouraging the use of modern irrigation methods (e.g., drip/sprinkler) for agricultural water management.

questions.solution: The Jal Kranti Abhiyan aims to strengthen water security by actively involving local communities in water management programs. A major objective is to promote water conservation and implement artificial recharge techniques to combat depleting groundwater levels. Additionally, the campaign focuses on encouraging farmers to adopt modern and efficient irrigation methods, such as drip and sprinkler systems, to optimize agricultural water usage and reduce wastage, ultimately ensuring the sustainable availability of water resources across different regions of India.

questions.text_english: Explain the concept of 'Humanisation of Nature' by giving examples.

key_points: Human intelligence and technology enable modification of natural environment.
Shift from being slaves to nature to masters of it.
Examples: Agriculture, industrialization, building cities, and dam construction.

questions.solution: The concept of 'Humanisation of Nature' or possibilism suggests that humans, through their growing intelligence and technological advancements, are no longer passive slaves to nature but active modifiers of it. Humans understand natural laws, such as friction and heat, to create technologies like fire, agriculture, and high-speed transport. For example, humans have transformed vast forests into agricultural landscapes, built large urban centers, and constructed dams on rivers to control floods and generate electricity. This demonstrates that humans have gained the ability to shape their surroundings, thereby 'humanizing' the natural environment according to their developmental needs.

questions.text_english: Suggest any three measures to solve the problem of 'Urban Waste Disposal' in India and explain them.

key_points: Waste segregation at the source (biodegradable and non-biodegradable).
Promotion of recycling and composting facilities.
Public awareness and community participation in sanitation drives.

questions.solution: Addressing urban waste disposal in India requires immediate and effective measures. First, source segregation is essential, where households must separate biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste to facilitate efficient processing. Second, municipal authorities should invest in recycling centers and composting plants to convert organic waste into fertilizer, significantly reducing the volume sent to landfills. Finally, raising public awareness through community engagement and education on responsible disposal practices is critical to changing social attitudes, which would reduce littering and encourage the adoption of systematic waste management procedures in urban neighborhoods.

(a) Which organisation publishes the 'Human Development Report' every year? Explain the four pillars of human development'.
OR
(b) Which country has the highest rank in the world in Human Development Index' in 2020? Explain four approaches of human development.

key_points: UNDP (United Nations Development Programme) publishes the report.
Four pillars: Equity, Sustainability, Productivity, and Empowerment.
Brief explanation of each pillar (e.g., Equity means equal opportunity).

questions.solution: The Human Development Report is published annually by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). Human development is built upon four fundamental pillars: Equity, Sustainability, Productivity, and Empowerment. Equity refers to ensuring equal access to opportunities for all individuals, regardless of their background. Sustainability emphasizes the need to preserve resources for future generations, ensuring development does not deplete the environment. Productivity focuses on investing in people to enhance their capabilities, thereby increasing their contribution to the economy. Finally, empowerment refers to granting people the freedom and agency to make decisions that influence their own lives. Collectively, these pillars provide the framework for achieving comprehensive human development globally.

questions.text_english: Describe any five features of commercial livestock rearing in the world.
questions.solution: Commercial livestock rearing is a highly organized, capital-intensive activity primarily found in developed regions. First, it is conducted on large, permanent ranches that are fenced to keep animals in designated areas. Second, it involves scientific and systematic management, including controlled breeding and health care. Third, farms specialize in raising a single type of animal, such as sheep for wool or cattle for beef, maximizing efficiency. Fourth, the operation is geared entirely toward global export markets, emphasizing product standardization. Finally, it requires significant investment in infrastructure, such as modern transport and storage facilities, to ensure products reach international markets in optimal condition.

key_points: Crucial for weather forecasting and disaster management.
Communication in remote and inaccessible areas.
Impact on education, telemedicine, and media.

questions.solution: Satellite communication has revolutionized global connectivity by providing instantaneous information exchange. Its primary importance lies in bridging the digital divide, allowing communication in remote and inaccessible terrains where traditional infrastructure like cables is unfeasible. For example, satellite data is indispensable for accurate weather forecasting and disaster management, such as tracking cyclones to save lives. Furthermore, it supports modern education through distance learning and has transformed healthcare via telemedicine, allowing doctors to provide consultation from afar. Finally, it plays a vital role in national defense and monitoring natural resources, illustrating its multifaceted role in the contemporary interconnected global society.

questions.text_english:
(a) Explain any five measures for the conservation of mineral resources in India.
OR
(b) Explain the importance of solar energy in Indian context.

key_points: Using minerals in a planned and sustainable manner.
Developing substitute materials (e.g., plastics/ceramics for metal).
Adopting better extraction technologies to minimize waste.

questions.solution: To conserve India's finite mineral resources, several strategies must be implemented. First, resources should be utilized in a planned and sustainable manner to prevent wasteful exploitation. Second, recycling and reusing metallic minerals, such as iron, copper, and aluminum, must become standard practice to reduce the demand for fresh extraction. Third, developing and utilizing substitute materials, like high-quality plastics or ceramics, can reduce dependence on critical metal ores. Fourth, the adoption of modern, efficient mining technologies can drastically minimize waste during extraction and processing. Finally, strict environmental regulations and responsible management during mining operations are necessary to preserve the ecological balance while ensuring long-term resource availability.

(a) "Pipelines are the most convenient and efficient mode of transportation in India." Examine the statement with examples.
OR
(b) "India has the second largest road networks in the world." Examine the statement with examples.

key_points: Low operating cost and energy efficiency.
Ideal for liquids and gases (e.g., oil, gas, slurry).
Essential for connecting refineries and urban supply centers.

questions.solution: Pipelines represent a highly convenient and efficient mode of transportation for specific commodities in India. Unlike rail or road transport, pipelines allow for continuous, uninterrupted movement of liquids and gases, which reduces the reliance on fuel-intensive vehicles. For instance, the Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) natural gas pipeline is vital for providing energy to industries and cities across northern India. They are cost-effective, energy-efficient, and immune to surface traffic congestion, making them ideal for long-distance transport of oil, natural gas, and slurry. Their ability to deliver resources directly from supply sources, such as offshore wells or refineries, to inland demand centers highlights their critical role in India's industrial infrastructure.
